title: Dynamic Throttle & Auto-Refund Playbook: adaptive overage mitigation and rollback
creator: Sana Li
description: PRD for an integrated throttling + automatic refund/rollback flow that reduces customer surprise charges during transient spikes while preserving safety and SLOs. This document defines requirements, acceptance criteria, and a phased rollout for: per-plan adaptive throttles, soft grace windows, automatic micro-refunds for short overages, and operator controls for manual rollback.
goals: Limit customer invoice surprises from short sudden spikes without allowing sustained over-usage
Provide deterministic, auditable refund behavior tied to entitlements and burst windows
Expose safe operator controls to pause/override automated rollbacks
Keep end-to-end latency impact to <5% for throttled requests and maintain existing SLOs
requirements: Per-plan burst allowance that can be consumed without immediate billing until grace window expires
Automatic detection of transient overage (configurable window: default 10 minutes) and issuance of micro-refunds if usage returns under entitlement within window
Configurable soft-throttle thresholds with progressive response: 1) warn, 2) soft-throttle (rate cap), 3) hard-throttle (reject), mapped per plan tier
Audit trail for each automated refund/rollback with reason, amount (tokens/credits), effective time, and linked request ids
Console UI for finance/ops to view recent rollbacks, manually approve/reverse, and adjust plan-level grace parameters
API hooks for customers to opt into auto-refund behavior or select strict billing mode
Billing ledger integration to ensure refunds create a journal entry and appear on next invoice and in billing export feeds
Fallthrough safety: automated rollback must never exceed pre-configured monthly refund budget per account without operator approval
End-to-end testing harness for simulated spikes and post-run reconciliation checks
scope_in: Plan-level grace windows and burst credit accounting
Automated micro-refund engine (credit adjustments, ledger entries)
Per-route and per-model throttle mapping based on plan
Console views and operator controls for rollback history
API flag to opt customers into experimental auto-refund flow
scope_out: Price changes or long-term contract re-pricing
Automated legal notifications for refunds exceeding threshold (requires legal review)
Real-time bank refunds (we only adjust billing credits/journal entries)
acceptance_criteria: A1: For synthetic spike tests (90th pct spikes for 5 minutes) the system issues soft-throttle and creates a refund entry if usage falls back within 10 minutes; refund amount matches excess tokens within 1% accounting variance
A2: Refunds generate ledger entries visible in billing export and appear on invoice reconciliation for customer within next invoice cycle
A3: Console shows recent rollback events with filters by account, plan, time, and operator action; operator can toggle 'pause auto-refunds' per account and the toggle change is audited
A4: API opt-in flag overrides global behavior and can be toggled via customer API keys; documented rate-limit behavior matches PRD matrix
A5: Automated refunds are capped by pre-configured monthly refund budget; attempts to exceed budget produce an alert to Billing ops and fall back to soft-throttle without refund
A6: Latency impact of introducing soft-throttle path is <5% median increase across controlled test traffic; P95 change <10%
A7: Unit/integration tests cover reconciliation, edge-case over-counting, and idempotency of refund operations
A8: Security review completed and data access for refund logs conform to audit logging policy
rollout_strategy: Staged rollout: feature-flagged per-tier -> pilot with 10 enterprise customers -> expand to all customers with opt-in prompts -> default-on for lower-risk tiers after 8 weeks of stable operation
rollout_phases: Phase 0: Experimental behind internal flag; run with synthetic traffic
Phase 1: Pilot (10 accounts) with manual ops oversight; daily reconciliation
Phase 2: Beta opt-in for self-serve accounts; expose console controls
Phase 3: Default-on for trial and freemium tiers with telemetry-driven gating
Phase 4: Full rollout with GA and SLA updates
metrics: % of invoices with automated refunds (target <= 1.5% for GA tier)
refund volume as % of monthly revenue (should remain <0.5% for first 3 months)
number of manual overrides by ops (monitoring signal for false-positives)

decisions: D1: Default soft-grace window will be 10 minutes; configurable per plan
D2: Refunds are implemented as billing credits (journal entries) rather than direct bank refunds for GA
D3: Customers may opt-out of auto-refunds; opt-in default varies by tier (trial free tiers default-on)
D4: Hard-throttle threshold set to 3x plan baseline for safety, with upper bound enforced by infrastructure
